title: Find out whether an export of a screen recording changes picture earlier than the canvas does
goal: When a video is written out, the app reads each recording frame nearest a moment, while the editor shows the frame on screen at that moment. On a 30 frames a second file the two now agree, but on a screen recording that holds one picture for a while, the written file may show the next picture up to half that pause early. Not yet seen happen.
notes: Unreproduced; found while fixing the-frame-shown-at-a-whole-second-is-the-one-tha (2026-11-22). Readers: MovieFrameStream.frameAndSurface steps on while the next sample is at least as near the moment (nearest); MovieSweepGrid.arrived fills a grid frame with the latest sample starting no more than MovieSweepGrid.lateSampleMS (1ms) after it (on screen); MovieDecoder seeks with MovieRef.seekSlopMS (16ms) either way, which on the probe showed the on-screen frame. On CFR 30fps all three give frame N at N/30 s (Tests/PhotonzMediaTests/WholeSecondFrameTests.swift). For a VFR clip with samples at 0 and 1000ms, nearest at grid 600ms would be the 1000ms sample, on-screen the 0ms one. TestClip.write only writes evenly spaced frames, so a test needs a writer with chosen presentation times. MovieFrameStreamTests assert nearest-frame on purpose, so changing it is a decision about frame-rate conversion for 24/25/60fps sources too.
acceptance: A test against a real decode of a recording with uneven frame times (one picture held a second) says whether the export reader and the canvas reader show the same frame at every grid moment
If they differ, the export reader shows the frame on screen at the moment, as the canvas does, and the export still plays as smoothly
